arxiv-2104-05645.title: Guiding large-scale management of invasive species using network metrics Journal: a journal
arxiv-2104-05645.creator: Jaime Ashander, Kailin Kroetz, Rebecca Epanchin-Niell, Nicholas B. D. Phelps, Robert G. Haight, Laura E. Dee
arxiv-2104-05645.description: Abstract Complex socio-environmental interdependencies drive biological invasions, causing damages across large spatial scales. For widespread invasions, targeting of management activities based on optimization approaches may fail due to computational or data constraints. Here we evaluate an alternative approach that embraces complexity by representing the invasion as a network and using network structure to inform management locations.

arxiv-2202-01529.title: Comparative assessment of federated and centralized machine learning
arxiv-2202-01529.creator: Ibrahim Abdul Majeed, Sagar Kaushik, Aniruddha Bardhan, Venkata Siva Kumar Tadi, Hwang-Ki Min, Karthikeyan Kumaraguru, Rajasekhara Duvvuru Muni

Federated Learning (FL) is a privacy preserving machine learning scheme, where training happens with data federated across devices and not leaving them to sustain user privacy.

arxiv-2205-12971.title: RV-detected planets around M dwarfs: Challenges for core accretion models
arxiv-2205-12971.creator: M. Schlecker, R. Burn, S. Sabotta, A. Seifert, Th. Henning, A. Emsenhuber, C. Mordasini, S. Reffert, Y. Shan, H. Klahr
arxiv-2205-12971.description: Abstract Context. Planet formation is sensitive to the conditions in protoplanetary disks, for which scaling laws as a function of stellar mass are known. Aims. We aim to test whether the observed population of planets around low-mass stars can be explained by these trends, or if separate formation channels are needed. Methods.

arxiv-2206-07057.title: Possibilities and Limitations of Kinematically Identifying Stars from Accreted Ultra-Faint Dwarf Galaxies
arxiv-2206-07057.creator: Kaley Brauer, Hillary Diane Andales, Alexander P. Ji, Anna Frebel, Mohammad K. Mardini, Facundo A. Gómez, Brian W. O’Shea
arxiv-2206-07057.description: Abstract The Milky Way has accreted many ultra-faint dwarf galaxies (UFDs), and stars from these galaxies can be found throughout our Galaxy today. Studying these stars provides insight into galaxy formation and early chemical enrichment, but identifying them is difficult.

arxiv-2305-07367.title: S-REINFORCE: A Neuro-Symbolic Policy Gradient Approach for Interpretable Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2305-07367.creator: Rajdeep Dutta, Qincheng Wang, Ankur Singh, Dhruv Kumarjiguda, Li Xiaoli, Senthilnath Jayavelu \affiliations Institute for Infocomm Research (IR), A*STAR, Singapore
arxiv-2305-07367.description: Abstract This paper presents a novel RL algorithm, S-REINFORCE, which is designed to generate interpretable policies for dynamic decision-making tasks. The proposed algorithm leverages two types of function approximators, namely Neural Network (NN) and Symbolic Regressor (SR), to produce numerical and symbolic policies, respectively.

arxiv-2307-02933.title: In Time and Space: Towards Usable Adaptive Control for Assistive Robotic Arms
arxiv-2307-02933.creator: Max Pascher, Kirill Kronhardt, Felix Ferdinand Goldau, Udo Frese, Jens Gerken
arxiv-2307-02933.description: Abstract Robotic solutions, in particular robotic arms, are becoming more frequently deployed for close collaboration with humans, for example in manufacturing or domestic care environments. These robotic arms require the user to control several Degrees-of-Freedom to perform tasks, primarily involving grasping and manipulating objects.

arxiv-2506-00918.title: Principled Input-Output-Conditioned Post-Hoc Uncertainty Estimation for Regression Networks
arxiv-2506-00918.creator: Lennart Bramlage, Cristóbal Curio
arxiv-2506-00918.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Lennart Bramlage, Cristóbal Curio. Uncertainty quantification is critical in safety-sensitive applications but is often omitted from off-the-shelf neural networks due to adverse effects on predictive performance. Retrofitting uncertainty estimates post-hoc typically requires access to model parameters or gradients, limiting feasibility in practice. We propose a theoretically grounded framework for post-hoc uncertainty estimation in regression tasks by fitting an auxiliary model to both original inputs and frozen model outputs.

pmc-10554285.title: SAT610 Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 1 - The First Reported Case In An Indigenous Australian
pmc-10554285.creator: Edward Mignone, Kirsten Neal
pmc-10554285.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Background: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 1 (MEN1) is a rare and under recognised syndrome. It has not been previously reported in Indigenous Australians for this reason. Clinical Case: A 48-year-old Indigenous Australian female was consulted on by an inpatient endocrine team in March 2020 for persistent hypercalcaemia on a background of a parathyroidectomy in 2011 for primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPTH). She was admitted to a remote Australian hospital for investigation and management of acute on chronic abdominal pain.

pmc-10646962.title: Diabetes and bacterial co-infection are two independent risk factors for respiratory syncytial virus disease severity
pmc-10646962.creator: Hakan Sivgin, Sirin Cetin, Ayse Ulgen, Wentian Li
pmc-10646962.description: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is common among older adults hospitalized with lower respiratory tract infection, yet information on the impact of DM on disease severity is limited. This study retrospectively analyzed 46 Turkish patients infected with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), with information on their comorbidities, co-infection status, and symptoms.

pmc-10690136.title: Insights into a co-precursor driven solid-state thermal reaction of ferrocene carboxaldehyde leading to hematite nanomaterial: a reaction kinetic study†
pmc-10690136.creator: Manisha Chakraborty, Sani Kundu, Ashis Bhattacharjee
pmc-10690136.description: Thermal decomposition of a mixture of ferrocene carboxaldehyde and oxalic acid dihydrate in O2 atmosphere produced rod-like hematite nanomaterial. The decomposition reaction was complex as evident from the overlapped multistep reaction steps in the non-isothermal thermogravimetry (TG) profiles obtained in the 300–700 K range. A peak deconvolution method was applied to separate the overlapped reaction steps.

pmc-12406481.description: Nitrogen (N) is essential for the physiological metabolism, growth, and development of plants. However, the mechanisms underlying the regulation of N absorption and utilization in apple remain unclear.

pmc-12779459.title: Transfer of microorganisms to and from textiles in healthcare settings: a systematic review
pmc-12779459.creator: Natalie Gassmann, Visar Vela, Walter Zingg, Aline Wolfensberger
pmc-12779459.description: Objective:Microbial contamination of textiles in healthcare settings is common and hypothesized to contribute to pathogen transfer. This systematic literature review aims to summarize the current evidence on microorganism transfer to and from textiles in healthcare and on factors that influence transfer.Design:Systematic literature review.Methods:Cochrane, Medline/Ovid, EMBASE, and Web of Science were searched.

pmc-13246176.title: Through the Prism: Shining Light on LGBTQIA+ Applicant Identities and Influences
pmc-13246176.creator: Kayla Iuliucci, Lea Moujaes, David Rudolph, Peter Fredericks, Blake Denley, Samuel Paskin, Arlene S Chung, Jaime Jordan, Edgardo Ordonez, Laura Smylie, Simiao Li-Sauerwine, P Logan Weygandt
pmc-13246176.description: IntroductionProgram diversity impacts rank-list creation for emergency medicine (EM)-bound applicants, but how lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer or questioning, intersex, asexual, and other sexual and gender minorities (LGBTQIA+) identities influence residency selection is unknown. This study investigates general patterns in EM applicant LGBTQIA+ identities, disclosure of those identities, and how LGBTQIA+ factors impact residency selection.
